title: compact: re-upsert after expire still folds is_stale=true (br-h7c-found)
description:
Discovered by br-h7c proptest_compact_preserves_materialized_state.

Minimal failing input:
  Upsert("b")
  Expire("b")
  Upsert("b")
  (then Compact)

Live DB materialized state after replay: b is live (is_stale=0).
After Compact + rebuild: b is stale (is_stale=1).

Root cause: src/commands/compact.rs::execute_with_paths walks the event log
and builds `expire_ids: HashSet<String>` of every id that ever appears in
an expire event. If the set contains the id, the compacted Upsert is
emitted with is_stale=true — regardless of whether a *later* Upsert
re-added the entry (re-add path).

Fix sketch: track last_op per id (max(entry_last, expire_last)). Fold
is_stale=true only when expire_last > entry_last. The permanent
+force-expire regression test (test_cmd_compact_permanent_entry_with_force_expire_is_marked_stale)
still passes because there's no re-upsert after the expire.

Tighter generator restriction applied in the proptest as workaround
(well_formed_sequence filter drops re-upserts after expire). Remove the
filter once this bug is fixed.

Discovered by: br-h7c
Found in commit: SHA TBD on cluster-opus (br-47d predecessor 58e364bf)
close_reason: Fixed: compact now tracks expire_last by index, folds is_stale only on last-write-wins. Regression test + 4096-case proptest pass. Commit 5c3da4e5.

title: T2: Bug 4 (MAJOR semantics) — blame scope to commits-that-touched-file
description:
See .omc/plans/kb-stale-check-fixes.md §T2

extract_blame_shas currently runs git blame --porcelain <file> and emits SHAs from entire file history. Wrong semantics — should be commits that touched the file.

What:

- Implementation: git log --pretty=%H -- <file> (deduped via HashSet).
- Update porcelain-parsing unit tests to log-format tests.

close_reason: T2 landed on fix/kb-stale-check (72d589b). extract_blame_shas → commits_that_touched_file using git log --pretty=%H -- file. 5 tests pass (3 parse_log_hashes + 2 fixture-based commits_that_touched_file tests asserting set disjointness between file histories). 74 total lib tests pass.

title: T3: Bug 3 (MAJOR perf) — SQL index + fast-path + hoisted prepare
description:
See .omc/plans/kb-stale-check-fixes.md §T3

All path lookups are full table scans. No index on entries.path. Leading-wildcard LIKE defeats any index. conn.prepare() called inside per-file loop.

What:
- Add CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entries_path ON entries(path) to ensure_schema in src/components/db.rs.
- Split path matching into two queries:
  - Fast path (uses index): WHERE path = ?1 AND is_stale = 0.
  - Substring fallback (full scan, only on cache miss): WHERE (path LIKE '%' || ?1 || '%' ESCAPE '\\' OR ?1 LIKE '%' || path) AND is_stale = 0.
- Hoist both Statement preparations outside file loop; reuse via query_map per file.
- Verify migration on existing DB.

Done when:
- EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on fast-path shows SEARCH USING INDEX idx_entries_path.
- EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on substring fallback still scans (expected).
- stale-check with 100 entries × 26 files runs fast path in O(file_count × log(N)).
close_reason: T3 landed on fix/kb-stale-check (da610b7). idx_entries_path added in ensure_schema. Fast-path query split out (uses index per EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN test); substring fallback unchanged behavior. Both prepares hoisted outside file loop (52 prepares → 2 for a 26-file request). 75 lib tests pass.

title: T4: Bug 2 (MAJOR perf) — dedupe + git rev-list --count
description:
See .omc/plans/kb-stale-check-fixes.md §T4

commits_since spawns one git log --oneline VERSION..HEAD -- path per matched row. 26 files × ~60 entries ≈ ~1500 subprocesses × ~5ms = ~7s fork/exec overhead. --oneline materializes commit messages just to count them.

What:
- Collect (version_ref, stored_path) tuples from matched rows into HashSet before invoking git.
- Replace git log --oneline VERSION..HEAD -- path with git rev-list --count VERSION..HEAD -- path.
- Cache count per tuple; reuse for every entry sharing that tuple.

Done when:
- Reproducer (26-file blame=true against normatix) completes in < 500ms.
- Subprocess-count assertion test: N entries sharing 4 distinct (version_ref, path) tuples → exactly 4 git invocations.
close_reason: T4 landed on fix/kb-stale-check (821c5f2). commits_since now uses 'git rev-list --count' (single integer output) instead of 'git log --oneline'. Per-tuple memoization via HashMap<(version_ref,path), Option<usize>>. Reproducer (26-file blame=true vs normatix): 404ms wall-clock — under epic 500ms criterion. 77 lib tests pass.
